x: May 16 · 100m · 10.67 · 1st. · C.Palace · Philips International Night of Athletics (McFarlane U.K. 1081, Quarrie Jam 10.95)

He was well clear of McFarlane (Haringey(UK) who then, however, got the better of Ernie in the 200 metres with 21.67 to 22.10. A week later at Christchurch Ernie's 200 metre time was down to 21.73 but he filled 3rd spot to the two UK men in both sprints.

On June 29th at Porsgrunn in the Telemark Games he defeated Jamaica's Don Quarrie and the U.K's Drew McMaster - all 10.2 - and then two days later in Oslo at the world famous Bislett Stadium, headed the U.K. trio of Sharp, McMaster and McFarlane to win in 10.47.
Ernie had to be content with 3rd. place behind Lattany and McFarlane, clocking 10.51 in the process. Ex-Surrey man Colin Gaynor was 5th in 10.65.

Both men dipped under Stu's recent mark and the middle distance record spree was truly underway.(1 Theriot 3.41.28 2 Hutchings 3.41.33 5 J Gladwin 3.41.45 6 G Staines 3.41.76).Ernie Obeng ran as a guest in the 100m placing 2nd to McFarlane in 10.5.

He snapped away from the blocks to win his heat easing up in 10.45 into a slight headwind - but what a pity the start of the final was such a shambles with McFarlane getting a clear flyer and the race not being recalled by the starter.

John McFarlane of Thames was his only opposition as they dropped down out of the woods near the end of the first lap, but before the loop past the lake had been completed, Phil had pressed the accelerator gently to the floor and was away.
Sure enough, with only 400 metres of the race gone, three men had already gained a 30 metre break - John McFarlane of Thames, Alistair Moses of Reigate and our own Phil.
Approaching the finish some way down on Thames’ John McFarlane, he sped round the oval to hand over with a two second lead, setting the fastest time of the day.
Stephen was into 4th … and then 3rd as he overtook McFarlane of Thames but then ran out of race before Herne Hill’s Dave Taylor could be reached.
